title: Event-Driven E-Commerce Microservices
description: NestJS monorepo where services talk over Kafka and business logic is decomposed into atomic Steps
longDescription: A pnpm monorepo of seven NestJS services behind a single API Gateway, communicating internally over Kafka instead of HTTP. Two decisions shape it: a shared packages/domain package is the only source of truth for inter-service contracts, and business logic is broken into single-responsibility Steps so services orchestrate rather than perform.

data.label: Customers App
data.description: Next.js storefront — the only external caller
data.details: App Router client under clients/. Talks REST to the gateway and never touches Kafka or a service directly.

data.label: API Gateway
data.description: The single REST surface; everything behind it is Kafka
data.details: Translates external REST calls into Kafka request-response or fire-and-forget event emission. Keeping this boundary strict is what lets services be added or split without changing the public contract.

data.label: Kafka
data.description: Internal transport for every service-to-service call
data.details: Runs with Zookeeper and kafka-ui in Docker Compose. Carries both request-response exchanges and emitted domain events, so a service can be consumed synchronously or reacted to asynchronously without a second transport.

data.label: packages/domain
data.description: Shared contracts — the source of truth between services
data.details: Every DTO, event payload and message pattern lives here. A service never redeclares a contract locally, which is what keeps a Kafka-based system from drifting into incompatible payloads.

data.label: Users
data.details: Built around the Steps pattern: HashPasswordStep, FindUserByEmailStep, CreateUserStep. The service orchestrates them — it conducts, it does not perform.

data.label: Products
data.details: Owns product data and publishes change events that inventory and checkout react to.

data.label: Inventory
data.details: Consumes product and checkout events to adjust stock, rather than being called synchronously during checkout.

data.label: Checkout
data.details: Coordinates the purchase flow across inventory and payments through events, so a failure in one participant does not roll back a distributed transaction synchronously.

data.label: Payments
data.details: Emits payment outcome events that checkout and email consume independently.

data.label: Email
data.details: Pure consumer — it subscribes to domain events and sends mail. No other service knows it exists, which is the practical payoff of event-driven decoupling.

data.label: users-db
data.details: Each service owns its storage; nothing reads another service's tables. Defined in Docker Compose with a pg_isready healthcheck so dependent containers start in order.

data.label: Docker Compose
data.description: The whole stack as one local environment
data.details: Brings up the broker, its coordinator, the UI and the database on a shared bridge network, with named volumes for anything that must survive a restart.

data.label: kafka-network
data.description: Private bridge network joining every service
data.details: Services address each other by container name on this network. Only the ports explicitly published reach the host, so the broker is not exposed by accident.

data.label: Zookeeper
data.details: Kafka's coordinator in this setup. It is infrastructure, not application code: no service talks to it directly.

data.label: Kafka broker
data.details: Carries both request-response exchanges and emitted domain events. Adding a consumer needs no change to the producer.

data.label: kafka-ui
data.description: Topic and message inspection during development
data.details: A browser UI over the broker, so a failing flow can be traced by reading the actual messages instead of guessing from logs.

data.label: users-db
data.details: postgres:16-alpine with a pg_isready healthcheck, so dependent containers wait for it to actually accept connections rather than merely having started. Credentials come from the environment with development defaults.

data.label: Named volumes
data.details: Broker state and database files live outside the containers, so recreating a container does not discard topics or rows.

keyFeatures.title: Services conduct, Steps perform
keyFeatures.description: Business logic is decomposed into single-responsibility Steps — HashPasswordStep, FindUserByEmailStep — that a service orchestrates. It is the discipline that keeps services from turning into fat services.

keyFeatures.title: One shared source of truth for contracts
keyFeatures.description: Every DTO, event payload and message pattern lives in packages/domain. No service redeclares a contract locally, which is what keeps a Kafka system from drifting into incompatible payloads.

keyFeatures.title: Kafka carries everything internal
keyFeatures.description: Both request-response exchanges and emitted domain events travel on one transport, so a service can be consumed synchronously or reacted to asynchronously without a second mechanism.

keyFeatures.title: Database per service
keyFeatures.description: Each service owns its storage and nothing reads another service's tables. Compose brings up Postgres with a pg_isready healthcheck so dependants start in order.
